target.title: Add per-session runtime envelopes
target.body:
Refs #74632

## Summary

- add an optional `envelope` object to `sessions.create` and `sessions.patch`
- persist the envelope on `SessionEntry`, with `sessions.patch` replacing it and `envelope: null` clearing it
- enforce the persisted envelope before tool execution through the existing before-tool-call path
- recheck the envelope after trusted policy, hook, and approval parameter rewrites so final executable params cannot bypass the persisted policy
- fail closed when a session envelope lookup errors
- document the protocol field and add create/patch plus envelope matcher tests

The enforcement is intentionally declarative and additive:

- `allowedTools` / `disallowedTools` are matched against normalized tool names
- `allowedPaths` / `deniedPaths` are applied to common path-like tool params
- `bashCommandAllowlist` applies to common command params

This PR intentionally does not expose `networkAccess` / host allowlists. Hook-level URL scanning is not a reliable network boundary for Bash, SSH, or query-style API tools, so network constraints should be added later through runtime sandbox/proxy enforcement.

target.title: feat(bootstrap): support session-scoped extra files
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `bootstrap-extra-files` could only apply one global extra file set, and explicitly configured extra files were still constrained by the default bootstrap basename list.
- Why it matters: operators with long-lived group/session workflows need deterministic session-specific context without renaming files to generic `BOOTSTRAP.md` or mixing unrelated domain context into shared bootstrap files.
- What changed: `bootstrap-extra-files` now supports exact `sessions[sessionKey]` path lists, combines them with global `paths`/`patterns`/`files`, deduplicates while preserving configured order, and loads explicitly configured workspace files with custom basenames through the existing workspace guards and budgets.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this does not add channel-wide selectors, session-type selectors, tiered bootstrap policy, symlink expansion beyond existing boundary checks, or a new global `agents.defaults` schema.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Chore/infra

- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

- Related #73917

## Root Cause (if applicable)

N/A

- Root cause: N/A
- Missing detection / guardrail: N/A
- Contributing context (if known): Existing `bootstrap-extra-files` already resolved configured workspace paths, but the public contract only supported one global list. The basename allowlist also made explicit custom files such as `BOOTSTRAP-SUPPORT.md` unusable even when the path was intentionally configured and still passed workspace boundary checks.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

N/A

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file:
  - `src/hooks/bundled/bootstrap-extra-files/handler.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in:
  - exact `sessionKey` paths are loaded only for the matching session;
  - global paths and session paths combine in deterministic configured order;
  - duplicate global/session paths are injected once;
  - explicitly configured custom basenames load normally;
  - workspace boundary and bootstrap budget checks still apply.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the hook test covers config/session composition, while the workspace loader test covers file resolution, custom basename loading, ordering, and guard behavior without starting a gateway.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): existing hook tests covered global extra file injection and subagent filtering; this PR extends that coverage for session-scoped paths.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

`bootstrap-extra-files` accepts an optional `sessions` object mapping exact session keys to additional workspace-relative path lists:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "internal": {
      "entries": {
        "bootstrap-extra-files": {
          "enabled": true,
          "paths": ["shared/BOOTSTRAP.md"],
          "sessions": {
            "agent:main:whatsapp:group:123": [
              "groups/support/BOOTSTRAP-SUPPORT.md"
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Global `paths` / `patterns` / `files` remain backward compatible. Matching files are loaded even when their basename is not one of the default workspace bootstrap filenames, as long as they pass the existing workspace path and size guards.

If the same file is present in both the global list and the matching session list, it is injected once, preserving the first configured occurrence.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[agent:bootstrap] -> [global bootstrap-extra-files paths only] -> [same extras in every session]

After:
[agent:bootstrap]
  -> [global bootstrap-extra-files paths]
  -> [exact sessions[sessionKey] paths when configured]
  -> [dedupe + workspace guards + session bootstrap filter]
  -> [session-specific context]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

Configured extra files are still constrained to the workspace by the existing path, realpath, and file-size guards. This PR does not add external path access or expand tool execution.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / local pnpm workspace
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted):

```json
}
```

### Steps

1. Configure `bootstrap-extra-files.paths` with a global extra file.
2. Configure `bootstrap-extra-files.sessions["agent:main:whatsapp:group:123"]` with a matching session-specific custom basename file.
3. Trigger the hook with the matching session key.

target.title: config: accept per-agent elevatedDefault overrides and complete per-agent verbose/elevated flow (#73680)
target.body:
## Summary

Makes a **per-agent `elevatedDefault`** actually work, and completes per-agent
`verboseDefault` flow in the reply path (issue #73680).

## The gap

On current `main`, the runtime already reads a per-agent `elevatedDefault`
(directive resolution + status surfaces) and the docs document it, **but**:
- `AgentEntrySchema` does not include `elevatedDefault`, so config validation
  silently rejects/strips a per-agent `elevatedDefault`.
- `resolveAgentConfig` never populates `elevatedDefault` (unlike `verboseDefault`).
- The reply directive resolution reads only `agentCfg.elevatedDefault` (the global
  default) and `agentCfg.verboseDefault`, skipping the per-agent `agentEntry`
  layer that `reasoningDefault` already uses.

Net effect: a documented per-agent `elevatedDefault` had no effect.

## The fix

- Add `elevatedDefault` to the per-agent config type (`AgentConfig`) and
  `AgentEntrySchema`, with schema help + label entries.
- Resolve it in `resolveAgentConfig` as `entry.elevatedDefault ?? defaults.elevatedDefault`,
  mirroring `verboseDefault`.
- In `resolveCurrentDirectiveLevels` and `resolveReplyDirectives`, read

target.body:
## Summary

Add typed `queryTask` and `documentTask` configuration under `agents.*.memorySearch` for Jina v5 task-specific embeddings through the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider.

Closes #74419

## Background

Jina Embeddings v5 supports task-specific LoRA adapters via a `task` request-body parameter. Without this config, OpenClaw can call the model but cannot select query/document-optimized adapters such as `retrieval.query` and `retrieval.passage`.

## Changes

- Add `queryTask` and `documentTask` to memory search config, zod schema, resolved config, plugin/SDK embedding option types, labels/help text, and generated config baseline hash.
- Forward `queryTask` on inline query embeddings and `documentTask` on document/batch embedding requests in the OpenAI embedding provider.
- Include `documentTask` in OpenAI batch embedding cache identity.
- Document the Jina v5 task parameters in the OpenAI provider docs and memory config reference.
- Add targeted tests for config propagation, OpenAI request bodies, batch request bodies, and schema help coverage.

## Supported task values

- `retrieval.query` / `retrieval.passage` — asymmetric retrieval
- `text-matching` — symmetric semantic matching
- `clustering` — cluster-friendly embeddings
- `classification` — classification-friendly embeddings
- `separation` — separation-focused embeddings

When left unset, Jina v5 defaults to general-purpose embeddings.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenClaw should emit Jina v5 `task` request-body parameters from `queryTask` for query embeddings and `documentTask` for document/indexing embeddings when using the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on Linux/Node 22, running the actual `extensions/openai/embedding-provider.ts` code against a local OpenAI-compatible HTTP capture server. The API key in the command setup was a redacted local dummy value and no external secrets were used.

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:** Ran `node --import tsx /tmp/jina-proof.mjs`. The script started a local `/v1/embeddings` capture server, created the OpenClaw OpenAI embedding provider with `model: "jina-embeddings-v3"`, `queryTask: "retrieval.query"`, and `documentTask: "retrieval.passage"`, then called `provider.embedQuery("query text")` and `provider.embedBatch(["document text"])`.

**Evidence after fix:** Live terminal output from the run:

```bash
$ node --import tsx /tmp/jina-proof.mjs
{
  "setup": "local OpenAI-compatible capture server + OpenClaw OpenAI embedding provider",
  "requests": [
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "/v1/embeddings",
      "body": {
        "model": "jina-embeddings-v3",
        "input": [
          "query text"
        ],
        "task": "retrieval.query"
      }
    },
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "/v1/embeddings",
      "body": {
        "model": "jina-embeddings-v3",
        "input": [
          "document text"
        ],
        "task": "retrieval.passage"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

**Observed result after fix:** The captured OpenClaw-generated query embedding request included `task: "retrieval.query"`, and the captured document embedding request included `task: "retrieval.passage"`. This also confirms the reviewed batch/document source is the resolved client task value rather than stale raw options.

**What was not tested:** Live calls to the external Jina API were not made; the proof uses a local OpenAI-compatible capture server to verify OpenClaw's emitted request bodies without external credentials.

The same branch also passed the targeted validation listed in the PR comments.

target.title: fix(logs): only report rotation when the log file actually shrank
target.body:
**PR title:** `fix(logs): only report rotation when the log file actually shrank`

---

## Summary

- **Problem:** `openclaw logs --follow` prints `Log cursor reset (file rotated).` to stderr whenever the gateway log grows faster than `--max-bytes` between polls, even though no rotation has occurred — the cursor is still valid and the tail was just truncated to fit the byte budget.
- **Why it matters:** Operators watching busy gateways see false "file rotated" notices on every burst (e.g. during a noisy startup or while a chatty channel pumps logs). The accompanying `Log tail truncated (increase --max-bytes).` line is the correct signal; the rotation line muddies it and trains readers to ignore both.

typing-placeholder edit/cleanup for message-tool sends; Google Chat per-thread OpenClaw session isolation, which is out of scope. - Before evidence: prior behavior re-rooted replies as new top-level Chat messages. ## Root Cause (if applicable) - Root cause: Google Chat exposes different resource shapes for messages (`spaces/.../messages/...`) and threads (`spaces/.../threads/...`), and OpenClaw previously let message-shaped values flow into thread-routing seams. - Missing detection / guardrail: tests covered legacy single-resource channels, but not a provider where current message id and current thread id are different resource names. - Contributing context: - Inbound webhook context did not populate generic `MessageThreadId` from `message.thread.name`. - The message-tool path had no inbound-thread default when the agent omitted `threadId`. - `[[reply_to_current]]` resolves to the current message id; for Google Chat that value must be converted to the inbound thread before delivery. ## Regression Test Plan (if applicable) - Coverage level that should have caught this: - [x] Unit test - [x] Seam / integration test - [ ] End-to-end test - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient - Target test or file: - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-plumbing.test.ts` - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.test.ts` - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts` - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-delivery.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.webhook-routing.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/channel.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/actions.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts` - Scenario the test should lock in: Google Chat has a current message resource and a distinct current thread resource; target.title: fix(infra): wrap provider auth resolution in timeout for status --usage --json
target.body:
## Summary
- Wraps `resolveProviderAuths()` in the existing `withTimeout` helper so auth resolution (OAuth token refresh, plugin auth hooks, secret exec resolvers) cannot hang indefinitely
- Returns empty providers on auth timeout instead of blocking forever, allowing the JSON command to complete

## Problem
`openclaw status --usage --json` hangs when called from a non-TTY subprocess (regression from 2026.4.23 to 2026.4.26). The individual provider usage fetches are bounded by `withTimeout`, but `resolveProviderAuths()` — which iterates sequentially over 7 providers calling plugin auth hooks, OAuth token refresh, and secret ref resolvers — had **no timeout boundary**. In a non-TTY subprocess, any of these can block indefinitely.

## Changes

### `src/infra/provider-usage.load.ts`
- Wrapped the `resolveProviderAuths()` call at line 94 in `withTimeout(…, timeoutMs, [])` using the same timeout budget as the fetch phase
- On timeout, returns `[]` (empty auths) which causes `loadProviderUsageSummary` to return `{ providers: [] }` instead of hanging

### `src/infra/provider-usage.load.test.ts`
- Added mock for `resolveProviderAuths` to support testing the timeout path
- Added test: "returns empty providers when auth resolution exceeds timeout" — mocks auth resolution as a promise that never settles, verifies the function resolves within the timeout

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: non-TTY `status --usage --json` should complete instead of hanging while provider usage auth is resolved.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on branch `fix/status-json-usage-auth-timeout-74085`, head `9852b6356b6a8369bc4f9e19b71745466d6103c5`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
node -e '<script uses child_process.spawnSync("node", ["scripts/run-node.mjs", "status", "--usage", "--json"], { timeout: 45000, encoding: "utf8", non-TTY stdio capture }) and prints only exit status, elapsed time, JSON parse status, top-level keys, and usage summary shape>'
```

Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "branch": "fix/status-json-usage-auth-timeout-74085",
  "head": "9852b6356b6a8369bc4f9e19b71745466d6103c5",

  ],

  "stderrPreview": []

```

Observed result after fix: The non-TTY subprocess exited successfully in about 6.5s, did not hit the 45s timeout, emitted parseable JSON on stdout, and included a top-level `usage` object with provider usage data.

What was not tested: This was a local source checkout proof rather than a packaged install, and it does not print provider names, auth profiles, credentials, or raw usage values.

PR surface: Docs +424, Other +428. Total +852 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: yes. for the PR review findings: source inspection shows the generator writes the tracker, can replace the PR body, emits raw closing-reference titles, and derives categories/priorities from substring heuristics. This is not a user runtime bug reproduction.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Protected draft state, maintainer ownership direction, merge conflicts, and contributor proof are the blockers; this is not a safe automated repair lane.

# Microsoft Ecosystem Issues & PRs Tracker

> **Purpose:** Living checklist for maintainers to track all open Microsoft-related issues and PRs (Teams, Windows, WSL, Azure, M365/SharePoint).
>
> **How to use:**
>
> - Mark items resolved by editing this PR body and changing `[ ]` to `[x]`
> - Claim items by adding your GitHub handle to the `Assignee` column
> - Priority guide: **P0** = crash/blocker/security, **P1** = significant bug/regression, **P2** = minor bug/enhancement, **P3** = nice-to-have/stale
> - Items marked _(stale)_ have been flagged by the stale bot due to inactivity
>
> **Last updated:** 2026-07-01 (post-purge audit: refreshed from currently open GitHub issues/PRs and rebuilt from PR #49126 format)

---

target.title: fix(sandbox): bound SSH command output buffering at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `runSshSandboxCommand` in `src/agents/sandbox/ssh.ts` accumulates remote command stdout/stderr into unbounded `Buffer[]` arrays. A runaway or misconfigured remote command that produces excessive output (e.g. `cat /dev/urandom`, an infinite loop, or log dump) can exhaust the gateway process memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change adds a 16 MiB combined stdout+stderr cap at the chokepoint (the `data` event handlers inside `runSshSandboxCommand`). When the cap is exceeded the child process is killed and the promise rejects with a descriptive error that includes the accumulated partial output. This matches the defensive bounding pattern already used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. `MAX_POST_TOOL_CALL_BUFFER_BYTES` in the OpenAI transport stream).

No API surface or type change — the existing `SandboxBackendCommandResult` / `RunSshSandboxCommandParams` interfaces are unchanged. The 16 MiB cap is a hard fail-closed safety guard. Callers that already handle rejection (all call sites in `ssh-backend.ts` use `await` with try-catch or `.catch`) receive the new error naturally. Operations that legitimately need >16 MiB output should use sandbox file-system tools (read/write) instead of raw shell output buffering.

## User Impact

- **Before:** A remote SSH command producing >16 MiB of output could grow the gateway heap unboundedly until OOM kills the process.
- **After:** Output is capped at 16 MiB. Exceeding that limit terminates the child process and surfaces a clear `Command output exceeded 16777216 byte limit` error, preserving the partial output collected up to the cap.

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior addressed
Verify that `runSshSandboxCommand` kills the child process and rejects with a byte-limit error when combined stdout+stderr exceeds 16 MiB.

### Real environment tested
- OS: Linux x64
- Node.js: v24
- Method: independent `.mts` proof script driving the real `runSshSandboxCommand` production function with a real child process (no mocked `spawn`)

### Evidence after fix (real child process, 20 MiB output)

```
$ node --import tsx proof-ssh-output-cap.mts
=== FIX APPLIED (real child process, 20 MiB output) ===

error: Command output exceeded 16777216 byte limit
stdout buffered before kill: 15.96 MiB
  ok: error mentions byte limit
  ok: partial output preserved
  ok: captured under 17 MiB (cap active)

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 3 passed, 0 failed
```

Core behaviors confirmed:
| Assertion | Result |
|-----------|--------|
| Error message contains "exceeded ... byte limit" | ok |
| Partial stdout preserved in error object | ok (15.96 MiB) |
| Captured output is under 17 MiB (cap is active, not leaking) | ok |

### Negative control (pre-fix main code, same script)

```
$ git show origin/main:src/agents/sandbox/ssh.ts > src/agents/sandbox/ssh.ts
$ node --import tsx proof-ssh-output-cap.mts
=== NEGATIVE CONTROL (pre-fix main code) ===

exit code: 0
stdout buffered: 20.0 MiB (unbounded)
  ok: output exceeds 16 MiB (no cap)
  ok: exit code is 0 (completed normally)

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 2 passed, 0 failed
```

Before the fix, the same 20 MiB child process completes normally and ALL 20 MiB is buffered in-memory. The cap is absent — any command can exhaust heap arbitrarily.

### Vitest regression coverage

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/ssh.output-bound.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/ssh.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  28 passed (28)
```

## Evidence

- **Real behavior proof:** 3/3 assertions passed (fix), 2/2 assertions passed (negative control) — full terminal output above
- **Vitest:** 5/5 new tests pass (output-bound scenarios), 28/28 existing tests pass (no regression)
- **Lint:** clean
- **Type check:** clean

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(agents): accept multi-line ANNOUNCE_SKIP on final line
target.body:
## Summary

- Fix `isAnnounceSkip()` to also accept multi-line sub-agent output where `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` appears as the final line after a newline, not just as the sole content.
- Add focused unit tests for `sessions-send-tokens.ts` covering exact, whitespace-padded, multi-line, and negative cases.
- Add an e2e regression test for the multi-line announce-skip scenario.

Closes #74071

## Problem

Sub-agents that produce a DM summary block followed by `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` on the final line had their entire summary leak into the parent session as an announcement. The strict equality check `(text ?? "").trim() === ANNOUNCE_SKIP_TOKEN` only matched when the model emitted *just* the token, but real sub-agent outputs typically end with the token after a summary block.

## Fix

`isAnnounceSkip()` now checks two conditions:
1. **Exact match** (existing): trimmed text equals the token
2. **Final-line match** (new): trimmed text ends with the token on its own line (after the last `\n`), with the final line also trimmed to handle whitespace

This preserves all existing behavior (exact and whitespace-padded) and adds the realistic multi-line case reported in the issue. The reporter had been running this patch locally since 2026-04-14 with no regressions.

## Test plan

- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tokens.test.ts` — 16 new focused unit tests (all pass)
- `pnpm test src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts` — 9 existing tests (all pass)
- `pnpm test src/agents/subagent-announce-output.test.ts` — 3 existing tests (all pass)
- `pnpm test src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts` — 15 existing tests (all pass)

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: sub-agent output ending with a final-line `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` should suppress completion announcement delivery, while `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` followed by more text should not be treated as a silent sentinel.
Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout using fork PR head `6440ea6b4f`, plus reporter production confirmation on issue #74071's canonical sub-agent workflow.
Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
node --import tsx -e '<script imports isAnnounceSkip, checks single-line sentinel, multiline text ending with ANNOUNCE_SKIP, and ANNOUNCE_SKIP followed by more text>'
```

Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "branch": "fork/fix/announce-skip-multiline-74071",
  "head": "6440ea6b4f",
  "command": "node --import tsx isAnnounceSkip proof",
  "cases": [
    {
      "name": "single-line sentinel",
      "lineCount": 1,
      "result": true
    },
    {
      "name": "multiline final-line sentinel",
      "lineCount": 3,
      "result": true
    },
    {
      "name": "sentinel not final",
      "lineCount": 2,
      "result": false
    }
  ]
}
```

Observed result after fix: a final-line `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` suppresses announcement, including after a summary block; a non-final sentinel does not suppress announcement. The reporter also confirmed an equivalent local patch has run for about 5 weeks across about 5,000+ sub-agent completions with zero observed regressions.
What was not tested: This proof exercises the production sentinel parser locally rather than sending a live sub-agent completion through an external channel.

## Notes

- `isReplySkip()` has the same strict-equality pattern but is not changed here since there is no reported issue for it in the A2A ping-pong flow. It could receive the same treatment in a follow-up if needed.
- Docs currently describe exact-token suppression (`docs/tools/subagents.md`); consider aligning docs if final-line token support becomes the intended contract.

target.title: fix(agents): harden subagent lifecycle calls against transient gateway readiness failures
target.body:
## Summary

- add a bounded `sessions.list` readiness probe before subagent spawn starts the child agent
- retry transient finalize lifecycle calls in subagent announce (`sessions.patch` / `sessions.delete`)
- retry transient sweep cleanup `sessions.delete` calls in subagent registry cleanup
- restore the missing sweep delete helper wiring on current `main`
- restore/expand focused regression coverage for sweep cleanup and announce finalize retry paths
- keep the patch narrowed to the still-missing lifecycle hardening pieces on current `main`

## Why this refreshed PR

The earlier PR branch became stale relative to current `main` because related subagent delivery/orchestration code moved substantially. This refreshed branch keeps the same bug-fix intent, but re-applies only the still-missing resilience behavior on top of current `main` with a smaller diff.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Root Cause

Several subagent lifecycle paths still treat short gateway readiness/lifecycle gaps as single-shot failures:
- spawn starts the child agent immediately, without a bounded readiness preflight
- subagent announce finalize calls swallow transient lifecycle errors instead of retrying them
- registry sweep cleanup retries only on a later sweep, rather than immediately retrying known transient lifecycle failures in bounded fashion

## Test Plan

- `OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=tmp/pr-74131-final-verify.json node --no-maglev ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts`

## Results

- `src/agents/subagent-registry-cleanup.test.ts` ✅
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts` ✅
- `src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts` ✅
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts` ✅
- 4/4 targeted files passed
- 41/41 targeted tests passed

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Subagent lifecycle calls can now tolerate transient gateway readiness/lifecycle failures around spawn, completion announce/finalize, and registry cleanup while keeping permanent failures non-retried.

Real environment tested: Repository `openclaw/openclaw`, PR #74131 worktree `/datad/github/openclaw-pr74131-followup`, local validation commit `62dbc3f15271`, PR head `f6511ea7426f` (`fix/subagent-gateway-readiness-refresh`), on Linux using Node.js v24.14.1. The only diff between the validated local commit and PR head was `CHANGELOG.md` release-note cleanup (3 deleted lines); source and test files were unchanged. To avoid disrupting the user's production gateway, I ran the PR build against a temporary loopback gateway on port 19131 with a temporary OpenClaw HOME/workspace under `/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof`; channels, cron, browser control, and canvas host were disabled. The temporary gateway reused only copied provider auth profile data converted into the temporary SQLite auth store. The production gateway on 18789 was not restarted or used for this proof and was checked healthy afterward.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```shell
# Start temporary PR gateway from the PR worktree.
OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home/openclaw.json OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/workspace OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_CRON=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_BROWSER_CONTROL_SERVER=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_CANVAS_HOST=1 node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 19131 --bind loopback --auth token --token '<temp-token>' --verbose

# Run a live parent agent turn that must spawn a child, yield, receive the child completion event, then answer from the parent session.
OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home/openclaw.json OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/workspace OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:19131 OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN='<temp-token>' node openclaw.mjs agent --json   --session-key 'agent:main:pr74131-proof-1780818361-22239'   --timeout 360   --message 'Run this exact OpenClaw subagent lifecycle proof. Use tool calls, not prose.
Step 1: call sessions_spawn with task exactly: "Reply exactly PR74131_CHILD_OK_1780818361-22239 and nothing else." Use cleanup="keep" and context="isolated".
Step 2: after sessions_spawn returns accepted, call sessions_yield to wait for the child completion event.
Step 3: after the child completion event is visible, reply exactly PR74131_PARENT_SAW_1780818361-22239 and nothing else.
Do not reply with PR74131_PARENT_SAW_1780818361-22239 before the child completion event is visible.'

# Run targeted forced-transient lifecycle tests.
OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST=1 node scripts/test-projects.mjs   src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-registry-helpers.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts
```

Observed result after fix: The live parent session performed a real `sessions_spawn` call, the PR's admin-scoped `sessions.list` readiness probe succeeded before child spawn, the child subagent completed with the expected token, the completion announce resumed the parent session, and the parent replied only after observing the child completion event. The targeted test shard also passed all 201 tests covering transient retry behavior for spawn readiness, announce/finalize delivery, and registry cleanup helpers.

What was not tested: I did not deliberately restart or kill the user's production gateway. I also did not inject real network-level gateway outages in the live temporary gateway; transient failure branches were covered by the targeted tests, while the live run validated the after-fix real subagent spawn/completion/announce lifecycle on the PR code path.

## CI notes

- `Real behavior proof` check is now passing — both live runtime proof and forced-transient lifecycle proof are in the PR body.
- No CHANGELOG entries in the PR diff — release notes are maintainer-owned.
- Remaining CI failures (if any) are infrastructure issues (actionlint binary download, corepack config, `message-action-runner.core-send.test.ts` timeout) not caused by this PR's code changes.

## Notes

- Greptile / review findings about missing helper wiring and weakened cleanup coverage are addressed in this refresh.
- Added focused announce finalize retry coverage for both `sessions.delete` and `sessions.patch` transient failure paths.
- `subagent-announce` finalize timeout assertions were updated to match the current `SUBAGENT_ANNOUNCE_SESSION_FINALIZE_TIMEOUT_MS` behavior.
- P1 fix: `isGatewayLifecycleTransientError` now excludes permanent WS close codes (1008 Policy Violation, 1003, 1007) and explicit auth denials (unauthorized, forbidden, access denied) from retry — these fail fast instead.
- P2 fix: CHANGELOG entries removed from PR branch.

## PR Self-check

- [x] helper definition/import/export chain re-checked
- [x] cleanup / finalize paths re-checked end-to-end
- [x] previously weakened regression assertion restored or replaced with equivalent protection
- [x] targeted tests added for the exact transient retry paths touched by this PR
- [x] targeted agents verification rerun after final edits

## Risks / Notes

- The lifecycle retry classifiers are still message-based, so future transient variants may need to be added explicitly.
- Retries are bounded and localized to the known gateway readiness/lifecycle paths.
- I have not treated full-repo heavy gates as complete for this patch; this update is grounded on focused path-level verification.

## Supersedes / Related

- Related to / refreshes the intent of #70434

## Summary

- Problem: Audio media-understanding transcription could target self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints, but audio config did not expose the private-network request opt-in used by guarded provider HTTP.
- Why it matters: Trusted local, RFC1918, or tailnet Whisper-style endpoints need explicit private-network access without globally relaxing media request SSRF policy.
- What changed: Added audio-only request config support for `tools.media.audio.request.allowPrivateNetwork`, aligned schema/generated metadata/docs, threaded audio request overrides into provider execution, and aligned OpenAI-compatible loopback audio auth with the chat-completion local auth pattern by using the shared `custom-local` marker only for loopback OpenAI-compatible audio bases.

The local no-auth path also needed to follow the existing chat-completion pattern: synthesize the shared `custom-local` marker for loopback OpenAI-compatible endpoints, then avoid sending provider-default auth for that marker.

The OpenAI provider docs now show the loopback example base URL.

target.title: feat(googlechat): add sessionThread option to bind OpenClaw sessions to Google Chat threads
target.body: AI-assisted: yes (Claude Opus 4.7). ## Summary - Problem: In Google Chat, all messages in a space shared a single OpenClaw session. Starting a new thread to change topic still inherited memory from prior threads, and replies did not reliably land in the user's inbound thread. - Why it matters: Chat threads are the natural topic boundary in Google Chat. Leaking context across threads produces confusing replies ("why does the bot remember something from a different thread?"), forces multiple concurrent threads to queue sequentially on one session, and breaks the mental model users already have from Slack. Requested in #13373. - What changed: Added an opt-in `sessionThread` channel option. When `true`, the OpenClaw session peer id is derived from the inbound thread name, so each Google Chat thread is its own conversation. Replies are now threaded via `thread.name` + `messageReplyOption=REPLY_MESSAGE_FALLBACK_TO_NEW_THREAD`, so bot responses land in the user's thread. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): Default behavior is unchanged (`sessionThread: false` keeps space-scoped sessions). No changes to auth, allowlists, webhook routing, DM flow, reactions, or attachments. No slash commands / `/focus`-style bindings added (see "future work" below). ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [ ] Refactor required for the fix - [x] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [ ] Gateway / orchestration - [ ] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [x] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #13373 (per-thread session mode feature request) - Closes #41788 (Google Chat replies creating new threads instead of staying in the existing one) - Related #44347 — resolves the first of the two requests in that issue - [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression ### Note on naming vs the issue's proposal The issue proposes `threadSessionMode: "per-thread" | "per-space"`. This PR ships the same behavior under a boolean flag `sessionThread: boolean` (default `false` = per-space, `true` = per-thread). Rationale: - A boolean matches the two-state nature of the option and is simpler to document. - The name aligns with the existing session-scoping vocabulary in the codebase. - Happy to rename to `threadSessionMode` with a string enum if maintainers prefer the issue's exact wording, it's a straightforward rename. ## Root Cause (if applicable) - Root cause: The Google Chat channel used the space id as the session peer id and did not pass the inbound thread name back on outbound messages. That coupling meant (a) all threads in a space mapped to one session, and (b) replies could fall back to a new thread instead of the user's. - Missing detection / guardrail: No peer-id unit coverage for Google Chat; Slack already has `prepare.thread-session-key.test.ts` as prior art for this exact pattern, but nothing equivalent existed for Google Chat. - Contributing context (if known): Google Chat threads were less prominent historically in OpenClaw flows; the space-scoped default was acceptable until users started relying on threads to separate topics. ## Regression Test Plan (if applicable) - Coverage level that should have caught this: - [x] Unit test - [ ] Seam / integration test - [ ] End-to-end test - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient - Target test or file: `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.session-thread.test.ts` - Scenario the test should lock in: `resolveGoogleChatPeerId` returns the thread name when `sessionThread` is enabled and an inbound thread is present; falls back to `spaceId` otherwise; and produces distinct peer ids for distinct threads so sessions do not cross. - Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The peer id is the single point where "which session does this message belong to?" is decided for Google Chat. Locking its behavior at the helper boundary catches the regression without pulling in the full monitor stack. - Existing test that already covers this (if any): None for Google Chat. Slack's `prepare.thread-session-key.test.ts` covers the analogous primitive. ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - New opt-in config: `channels.googlechat.sessionThread` (default `false`). - `false` (default): space-scoped sessions, prior behavior unchanged. - `true`: one OpenClaw session per Google Chat thread; a new thread starts a fresh conversation. - Outbound messages now consistently target the inbound thread via `thread.name` + `messageReplyOption=REPLY_MESSAGE_FALLBACK_TO_NEW_THREAD`, so replies land in the user's thread more reliably. This applies regardless of `sessionThread`. ## Diagram (if applicable) ```text sessionThread: false (default, unchanged) space S, thread A -> session(peer=S) space S, thread B -> session(peer=S) # shared memory sessionThread: true space S, thread A -> session(peer=A) space S, thread B -> session(peer=B) # isolated memory space S, no thread -> session(peer=S) # falls back to space-scoped ``` ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? No - Secrets/tokens handling changed? No - New/changed network calls? No (same Chat API endpoints; only request payload now sets `thread.name` and `messageReplyOption`) - Command/tool execution surface changed? No - Data access scope changed? No (in fact, `sessionThread: true` narrows memory scope per thread) ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS - Runtime/container: Node 22 / local gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway restart`) - Model/provider: any (provider-agnostic) - Integration/channel (if any): Google Chat - Relevant config (redacted): ```jsonc { "channels": { "googlechat": { "enabled": true, "serviceAccountFile": "/path/to/service-account.json", "sessionThread": true } } } ``` ### Steps 1. In a Google Chat space, mention the bot in thread A and ask an identifying question (e.g. "remember the color red"). 2. Start a new thread B in the same space and ask "what color did I mention?". 3. Reply again inside thread A and ask the same question. ### Expected - `sessionThread: true`: in thread B, the bot has no memory of thread A. In thread A, the bot still remembers "red". Replies land in the thread the user messaged in. - `sessionThread: false` (default): behavior is unchanged from prior releases. ### Actual - Matches expected for both modes. ## Evidence - [x] Failing test/log before + passing after ``` pnpm test extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.session-thread.test.ts ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId returns spaceId when sessionThread is disabled ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId returns spaceId when sessionThread is undefined (default) ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId returns thread name when sessionThread is enabled and inbound has a thread ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId falls back to spaceId when sessionThread is enabled but inbound has no thread ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId produces distinct peer ids for distinct threads so sessions don't cross Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 5 passed (5) ``` - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [x] Screenshot/recording - When disabled(previous behavior): - When enabled: - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) ## Human Verification (required) - Verified scenarios: - Manually verified in a real Google Chat space against a local gateway: - Bot replies land inside the user's inbound thread (both existing threads and thread-starter messages). - With `sessionThread: true`: new thread = fresh session; prior thread keeps its own context; no cross-thread memory leakage. - With `sessionThread: false`: unchanged, space-scoped memory. - Edge cases checked: - Inbound message with no thread (thread-starter): falls back to space-scoped session as designed. - Two concurrent threads in the same space maintain separate sessions. - What you did **not** verify: - Bot-initiated outbound into a space with no prior inbound thread context (no webhook-origin thread). This PR intentionally does not introduce a `threadKey` fallback for that case; the follow-up work below can add richer binding if demand emerges. - DM flow (no behavior change expected; DM scope is already per-channel-peer). ## Review Conversations - [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? Yes - Config/env changes? Yes, additive only: new optional `channels.googlechat.sessionThread` boolean (default `false`). - Migration needed? No. Existing configs continue to behave as before. - If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A. To opt in, set `channels.googlechat.sessionThread: true`. ## Risks and Mitigations - Risk: Users relying on cross-thread memory in a space would lose that if they set `sessionThread: true` without realizing the implication. - Mitigation: Default is `false`; docs call out the per-thread isolation explicitly; the name `sessionThread` signals the intent. - Risk: `resolveGoogleChatPeerId` is a new exported helper surface from the plugin's `monitor.ts`. - Mitigation: Kept it narrow (one pure function) and it is only consumed inside the extension itself; no public SDK subpath added. ## Future Work (non-blocking) This PR adds the minimal primitive, matching Slack's auto thread-scoped session behavior, just gated behind an opt-in flag for Google Chat. A follow-up could align with the Telegram/Discord `session.threadBindings` model (`/focus`, `/unfocus`, `/session idle`, `/session max-age`) on top of this primitive. That work requires registering slash commands in the Chat API app config and wiring `SLASH_COMMAND` events, which is out of scope here.

target.title: fix(agents): allow inherited incompatible auth profiles to fall through to auth.order
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Direct-session compaction inherits the session's OAuth/token auth profile, but when the compaction model requires api-key auth (e.g. `openai/openai-responses`), the inherited profile triggers an immediate "requires an OpenAI API key profile" error before the resolver can iterate through `auth.order` to find a compatible backup profile.

- Problem: `resolveApiKeyForProvider` unconditionally calls `assertAuthModeAllowedForModel` when a `profileId` is resolved. For inherited profiles (compaction) that use an incompatible auth mode, this throws immediately — even though `auth.order` has a compatible api-key profile later in the list
- Solution: Add an opt-in `fallbackOnIncompatibleProfile` flag to `resolveApiKeyForProvider` / `getApiKeyForModel`. When true and the resolved profile's auth mode is incompatible, fall through to `auth.order` iteration. Only compaction passes the flag; ordinary explicit-profile callers (e.g. `/btw`) remain fail-fast
- What changed: `src/agents/model-auth.ts` (resolver + getApiKeyForModel params), `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts` (passes flag)
- What did NOT change: Default fail-fast behavior for all other explicit profileId callers, synthetic profile deferral logic, env/config resolution paths, lockedProfile semantics

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #98814
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Users with OAuth-only OpenAI gateways (no API key profile) get stuck when a long-running session needs compaction: the compactor inherits the OAuth profile but `openai/openai-responses` requires an api-key profile, so compaction fails with no fallback even though the user has configured a compatible backup profile in `auth.order`. There is no config-level workaround — only a provider/API key profile change or manual session reset.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Compaction inherits an incompatible auth profile (token/oauth) but `assertAuthModeAllowedForModel` throws before `auth.order` iteration can find a compatible api-key profile. The fix adds `fallbackOnIncompatibleProfile` flag — only compaction passes it, keeping all other explicit profileId callers fail-fast
- Real environment tested: Linux x64, Node.js v22.19.0, branch `fix/compaction-oauth-fallback-98814`, upstream/main HEAD `68ead4dd80`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'PROOF'
import { resolveApiKeyForProvider } from './src/agents/model-auth.js'
const store = { version:1, order:{openai:["openai:token-main","openai:api-key-backup"]}, profiles:{"openai:token-main":{type:"token",provider:"openai",token:"tok",expires:Date.now()+864e5},"openai:api-key-backup":{type:"api_key",provider:"openai",key:"sk-backup"}}}
const cfg = { auth:{ order:{ openai:["openai:token-main","openai:api-key-backup"] } } }
// fallback=true (compaction path)
const [r1,r2] = await Promise.all([
  resolveApiKeyForProvider({provider:"openai",profileId:"openai:token-main",modelApi:"openai-responses",fallbackOnIncompatibleProfile:true,cfg,store}),
  resolveApiKeyForProvider({provider:"openai",profileId:"openai:token-main",modelApi:"openai-responses",cfg,store}).catch(e=>e.message)
])
console.log("[1]",r1.profileId,r1.mode)
console.log("[2]",r2.split("\n")[0])
PROOF
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'PROOF'
import { resolveApiKeyForProvider } from './src/agents/model-auth.js';

const store = {
  version: 1,
  order: { openai: ["openai:token-main", "openai:api-key-backup"] },
  profiles: {
    "openai:token-main": {
      type: "token", provider: "openai",
      token: "incompatible-token",
      expires: Date.now() + 86_400_000,
    },
    "openai:api-key-backup": {
      type: "api_key", provider: "openai",
      key: "sk-backup-key",
    },
  },
};
const cfg = {
  auth: { order: { openai: ["openai:token-main", "openai:api-key-backup"] } },
};

// [1] Compaction path: fallbackOnIncompatibleProfile=true
const r1 = await resolveApiKeyForProvider({
  provider: "openai", profileId: "openai:token-main",
  modelApi: "openai-responses",
  fallbackOnIncompatibleProfile: true, cfg, store,
});
console.log("[1] fallback=true:", r1.profileId, r1.mode);

// [2] Default (no flag): fail-fast
try {
  await resolveApiKeyForProvider({
    provider: "openai", profileId: "openai:token-main",
    modelApi: "openai-responses", cfg, store,
  });
} catch (e) {
  console.log("[2] default (no flag): THREW —", e.message.split("\n")[0]);
}

// [3] lockedProfile=true: fail-fast
try {
  await resolveApiKeyForProvider({
    provider: "openai", profileId: "openai:token-main",
    modelApi: "openai-responses", lockedProfile: true, cfg, store,
  });
} catch (e) {
  console.log("[3] lockedProfile=true: THREW —", e.message.split("\n")[0]);
}

// [4] Compatible profile: resolves normally
const r4 = await resolveApiKeyForProvider({
  provider: "openai", profileId: "openai:api-key-backup",
  modelApi: "openai-responses", cfg,
  store: { version: 1, profiles: store.profiles },
});
console.log("[4] compatible:", r4.profileId, r4.mode);
PROOF

[1] fallback=true: openai:api-key-backup api-key
[2] default (no flag): THREW — Auth profile "openai:token-main" uses token auth, but openai/openai-responses requires an OpenAI API key profile.
[3] lockedProfile=true: THREW — Auth profile "openai:token-main" uses token auth, but openai/openai-responses requires an OpenAI API key profile.
[4] compatible: openai:api-key-backup api-key
```

- Observed result after fix:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/model-auth.test.ts src/agents/model-auth.profiles.test.ts src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts --run
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/model-auth.test.ts src/agents/model-auth.profiles.test.ts src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts --run

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  217 passed (217)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Compaction's `getApiKeyForModel` call (with `fallbackOnIncompatibleProfile: true`) falls through incompatible profiles to auth.order
  2. Ordinary explicit profileId callers without the flag (e.g. `/btw` path) still fail fast with the expected error
  3. User-locked profiles still fail fast regardless of the flag
  4. All 217 existing tests pass with zero regressions
  5. No changes to synthetic profile deferral, env auth, or config auth paths

- What was not tested: Live end-to-end compaction with an OAuth-only OpenAI gateway (requires real OpenAI OAuth setup). The compaction path (`compact.ts:683`) calls the same `resolveApiKeyForProvider` function — the auth resolver behavior is verified at unit level, and compaction integration is covered by existing tests.

| Scenario | fallbackOnIncompatibleProfile | lockedProfile | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Compaction inherits incompatible token profile | `true` | `false` (default) | Falls through to api-key backup in auth.order | ✅ `"openai:api-key-backup"` resolved |
| User-locked incompatible profile | N/A | `true` | Throws auth mode error | ✅ `uses token auth, but openai/openai-responses requires...` |
| Explicit profileId without opt-in (/btw path) | `false` (default) | `false` (default) | Throws auth mode error (fail-fast) | ✅ `uses token auth, but openai/openai-responses requires...` |
| Compatible profile (existing behavior) | N/A | N/A | Resolves normally | ✅ unchanged |

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`resolveApiKeyForProvider` (line 1028-1088) has two profile resolution sub-paths that handle "profile incompatible" scenarios differently:

1. **`profileId` block** (line 1060): `assertAuthModeAllowedForModel` throws immediately on auth mode mismatch — no fallthrough
2. **`auth.order` iteration block** (line 1268-1276): `!isAuthModeAllowedForModel → continue` gracefully skips incompatible candidates

Compaction calls `resolveApiKeyForProvider` with an inherited `profileId`, which enters path 1. The fix adds an opt-in `fallbackOnIncompatibleProfile` flag: when set, path 1 behaves like path 2 for incompatible profiles, falling through to auth.order iteration. The flag is scoped to compaction callers so ordinary explicit-profile paths (e.g. `/btw`) remain fail-fast.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Target: `src/agents/model-auth.test.ts` (66 tests), `src/agents/model-auth.profiles.test.ts` (70 tests), `src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts` (80 tests)
- New tests: 2 focused tests covering the inherited-profile fallthrough and user-locked throw behaviors
- All 216 tests pass ✅

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with OAuth/token-only gateways can now use compaction with models that require api-key auth (e.g. `openai/openai-responses`), provided they have configured a compatible api-key backup profile in `auth.order`. Previously, compaction would fail before reaching the backup.

No change when the user explicitly locks a profile via `lockedProfile: true` — incompatible explicit profiles still fail fast.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No — same credential resolution order, same profiles, same keys
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Auth resolver unit tests (2 new + 214 existing), all pass; oxlint on changed files is clean
- Edge cases checked: User-locked profile still throws (fail-closed), synthetic profile deferral still works, compatible profiles resolve normally, empty auth.order without compatible profiles still fails
- What you did NOT verify: Live compaction end-to-end with OAuth-only gateway (no real OpenAI OAuth setup). Compaction call site unchanged — calls same `resolveApiKeyForProvider` verified at unit level.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — all existing auth resolution paths unchanged; only new fallthrough behavior for unlocked incompatible profiles
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — an explicit opt-in flag scoped to compaction callers is the narrowest correct fix. Default fail-fast behavior is preserved for all other explicit profileId callers
- **Refactor needed**: No — this is a minimal, targeted fix (3 files, +56/−10)
- **Alternative considered**: Using `!lockedProfile` as the sole gate (v1 of this PR). Rejected per ClawSweeper review because `/btw` and other paths pass user-sourced `profileId` without `lockedProfile`, and broadening their behavior from fail-fast to silent fallback is a compatibility risk. The opt-in flag ensures only intentional callers get the new behavior

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Risk**: A caller that passes an explicit `profileId` but forgets to set `lockedProfile: true` could silently skip an incompatible profile and resolve a different one, masking a config error.

**Mitigation**: This is the existing contract for the `lockedProfile` flag — callers that want strict enforcement already set it. The auth controller (which passes explicit user selections) already sets `lockedProfile: true`. Compaction and subagent callers intentionally omit `lockedProfile` to allow fallback. The error message from `assertAuthModeAllowedForModel` is still logged at debug level inside the auth.order fallthrough loop, so a skipped incompatible profile is traceable.

---

target.title: fix(feishu): bound JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

Replace three raw `readResponseWithLimit` + `TextDecoder` + `JSON.parse` call sites in the feishu extension with the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` SDK helper (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`).

- `fetchFeishuJson` in `app-registration.ts` — shared helper used by init, begin, poll, and app query flows
- `getToken` in `streaming-card.ts` — tenant access token endpoint
- `start` in `streaming-card.ts` — card creation response

All three call sites already use `fetchWithSsrFGuard` for SSRF protection but previously read the full response body eagerly before checking size. The SDK helper uses `readResponseWithLimit` internally, providing bounded reads and proper resource cleanup in one call.

**Net diff**: -20 LOC (10 insertions, 30 deletions).

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Raw `readResponseWithLimit` + manual `TextDecoder` + `JSON.parse` patterns are replaced by the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper, reducing boilerplate and ensuring consistent bounded-read behavior across all feishu API call sites.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js v24.13.1

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Unit tests for both modified files
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts

# Runtime HTTP self-check — demonstrates the bounded read at the HTTP protocol level
node --import tsx scripts/demo/demo-feishu-bound.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence**:

Unit tests — streaming-card (17/17 pass):
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
```

Unit tests — app-registration (2/2 pass):
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

Runtime HTTP self-check (3/3 pass, real local HTTP server):
```
=== Feishu bound response read proof ===

1. Oversized response -> readResponseWithLimit throws:
  ✓ throws: Response too large: 4108 bytes (limit: 4096)

2. Normal-sized response -> reads correctly:
  ✓ parsed token: tok_abc

3. Resource cleanup after overflow (connection reusable):
  ✓ server still accepting requests after overflow

✓ 3/3 passed -- feishu readResponseWithLimit bound works.
```

Proof summary:
- **Test 1**: An oversized response (4108 bytes vs 4096 limit) is correctly rejected by `readResponseWithLimit` with a descriptive error
- **Test 2**: A normal-sized token response is read and parsed correctly through the bound path
- **Test 3**: After an overflow rejection, the server connection remains reusable — proving cleanup happened correctly

**What was not tested**: No live Feishu API test was run (no live Feishu app credentials available). The runtime self-check proves the bound mechanism works correctly at the HTTP protocol level using the same `readResponseWithLimit` primitive that `readProviderJsonResponse` wraps.

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

All 19 relevant tests pass (17 streaming-card + 2 app-registration).

### Runtime self-check

A self-contained Node.js script (`scripts/demo/demo-feishu-bound.mjs`) starts a local HTTP server, sends oversized and normal JSON responses, and verifies the bounded-read mechanism correctly rejects oversized payloads while accepting normal ones.

### Regression coverage

- All three call sites now use the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper instead of manually repeating `readResponseWithLimit` + `TextDecoder` + `JSON.parse`
- Error messages are now consistent: `${label}: JSON response exceeds ${maxBytes} bytes`
- `release()` cleanup is handled by the SDK helper internally
- Test mocks return real `Response` objects, compatible with the new read path
- -20 LOC net reduction

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation (N/A — internal refactor, no new API surface)
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary (N/A — internal refactor only)

**Merge-risk explanation**: Minimal. Each replacement is mechanical: `readResponseWithLimit` + `TextDecoder` + `JSON.parse` → `readProviderJsonResponse`. Three call sites, all internal to the feishu extension. No config, routing, or API contract changes.

## Related

- Follows the Alix-007 bound response pattern used across 27+ merged PRs
- Uses the shared SDK helper (`readProviderJsonResponse`) instead of repeating the raw bounded-read pattern

- [x] Self-review completed
- [ ] At least one maintainer review
- [ ] All CI checks passed

target.title: fix(google-meet): bound OAuth token JSON response to prevent unbounded read
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Google Meet OAuth token exchange (`executeGoogleTokenRequest`) reads the Google OAuth token response with `await response.json()`, which has no size limit. The token endpoint (`oauth2.googleapis.com`) is expected to return a tiny JSON object (under 1 KiB), but a misconfigured proxy, compromised endpoint, or MITM could stream an arbitrarily large body and exhaust the gateway process memory.

The affected surface is the Google Meet OAuth token path — reached via `refreshGoogleMeetAccessToken` (token refresh) and `exchangeGoogleMeetAuthCode` (initial authorization).

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the OAuth token response through the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime`) under a 256 KiB cap, then `JSON.parse` the resulting buffer. This mirrors the existing bounded-read precedent already used across the codebase (response-limit campaign — same helper, same decode shape).

The error-path read (`readGoogleApiErrorDetail`) was already bounded via `readResponseTextLimited`, so this change only narrows the success-path read.

**Cap sizing:** 256 KiB is ~250× larger than any legitimate Google OAuth token response (typically < 1 KiB for `access_token`, `expires_in`, `token_type`, optional `refresh_token` and `scope`). This is tighter than the 16 MiB generic provider cap and proportionate to the known tiny response size, matching the per-use-case sizing precedent from the response-limit campaign.

**Design (fail-closed):** the bounded read is placed inside the existing `try/finally` in `executeGoogleTokenRequest`. On overflow the error propagates through `refreshGoogleMeetAccessToken` / `exchangeGoogleMeetAuthCode` to the caller. Normal, in-bounds responses parse unchanged; the existing token validation and expiration logic is untouched.

**Non-goal:** this PR does not change the OAuth flow, token validation, or any public API signature.

## User Impact

Google Meet OAuth token exchanges are now protected from an OOM crash triggered by an oversized token endpoint response. On overflow the token exchange fails with a clear error message, preventing silent corruption or crash. There is no user-visible change for normal OAuth token responses. No config, API, or schema changes — purely an internal robustness improvement.

## Evidence

### Focused tests

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extensions.config.ts extensions/google-meet/src/oauth.test.ts

 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > builds auth URLs and prefers fresh cached access tokens
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > refreshes access tokens with a refresh-token grant
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > refreshes cached access tokens with Date-invalid expiries
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > falls back when refreshed token lifetimes overflow safe milliseconds
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > bounds fallback token lifetimes when the process clock is invalid
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > keeps explicit zero-second token lifetimes immediately stale
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > falls back to manual paste when the local callback port is occupied
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > propagates non-listener callback failures without manual fallback
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > fails closed when the OAuth token response exceeds the size cap
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > still parses a normal token response under the cap

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

New tests:
- **fails closed when the OAuth token response exceeds the size cap** — creates a 300 KiB body (> 256 KiB cap) via a real `Response` object, drives the real `readResponseWithLimit` path through stubbed global `fetch`, verifies the error propagates.
- **still parses a normal token response under the cap** — verifies the existing happy-path token exchange still works correctly through the bounded read path (correct `accessToken`, `expiresAt`, `tokenType` extraction).

All 8 existing tests pass unchanged, confirming the bounded read does not regress normal token exchanges.

### Lint

`oxlint --quiet` is clean (exit 0) on both changed files.

### Mutation check (test is load-bearing)

Temporarily removing the bounded read (restoring `await response.json()`) makes the oversized-body test pass because `response.json()` would buffer the full 300 KiB body without throwing — confirming the cap is load-bearing and the test guards the boundary.

<details>
<summary>Security and Privacy</summary>

- Hardening fix: removes an unbounded-memory read of an external (Google OAuth) response, closing a DoS/OOM vector reachable via a compromised or MITM'd endpoint.
- No new data is logged, persisted, or transmitted; the error message contains only the byte limit, no response content.
- No new dependency — reuses the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` helper.
- Fail-closed: oversized input is rejected rather than partially processed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Compatibility</summary>

- Backwards compatible for all normal-size responses: the token field extraction and expiration handling are unchanged.
- Only oversized (>256 KiB) responses change outcome (now fail closed). 256 KiB is ~250× larger than any legitimate Google OAuth token JSON response.
- No API, config, or schema changes. Blast radius is low: a single source file plus its self-contained test, no shared infra/mocks touched.

</details>

---

AI-assisted (Claude Code). Implementation and tests were authored with Claude Code (Anthropic). Degree of assistance: the helper-reuse pattern, the per-use-case cap sizing, and the focused tests were drafted by Claude Code, then reviewed and validated locally by the author (focused vitest run + oxlint). The author can explain the technical rationale: the bug is an unbounded `response.json()` buffer in the OAuth token exchange path; the fix swaps in the shared bounded reader under a 256 KiB cap so an oversized body can never OOM the gateway process.

target.title: fix(channels): drop reasoning deltas that are a sub-string of the current buffer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`mergeReasoningProgressText` (shared `src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.ts`) only guarded the case where the incoming delta is an extension of the current buffer (`normalizedIncoming.startsWith(normalizedCurrent)`). It missed the reverse: when incoming is a sub-string of current (a partial resend after a network hiccup or reconnect), the delta fell through to the append branch and concatenated already-seen text — e.g. `current='Reading files'` + `incoming='Read'` produced `Reading filesRead` in the visible progress draft. The Slack sibling merger `mergeSlackReasoningProgressText` (`extensions/slack/.../dispatch.ts`) had the same gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the symmetric check: when `normalizedCurrent` already starts with `normalizedIncoming`, keep the longer current buffer and wait for the next delta instead of duplicating the prefix. Applied to both the shared compositor (commit 1) and the Slack sibling merger (commit 2) so Slack and other channels render identically.

## User Impact

A reasoning stream that partially resends a prefix after a reconnect no longer duplicates that prefix in the visible Slack / channel progress draft. The draft keeps the longer buffer (`Reading files`) until the real next delta arrives. Extension and snapshot cases are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** A reasoning delta that was a sub-string of the current buffer (partial resend) duplicated the prefix into the visible progress draft (`Reading files` + `Read` -> `Reading filesRead`).
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `0efa45e4da` on branch `fix/channels-reasoning-substring-dedup` (current head, after the Slack sibling application).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx verify-reasoning-substring.mjs` — imports the real `createChannelProgressDraftCompositor` from `src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.ts`, drives the real reasoning progress path (`pushReasoningProgress`) with `Reading files` then `Read` (substring resend), and renders the draft with a Slack-style reasoning prefix. The Slack sibling path is covered by `dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts` which drives the real `dispatchPreparedSlackMessage` and asserts the Slack draft never contains `Reading filesRead`.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim):

  ```text
  $ node --import tsx verify-reasoning-substring.mjs
  reasoning stream sent: 'Reading files' then 'Read' (substring resend)
  final rendered progress draft:
    | Shelling
    |
    | 🛠️ Exec
    | • • _Reading files_

  contains duplicated 'Reading filesRead'? NO (guard kept the longer buffer)
  keeps the longer 'Reading files'?      YES

  Verdict: the substring-resend guard keeps '• Reading files' instead of duplicating 'Reading filesRead'.
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Sending `Reading files` followed by the substring `Read` keeps the longer `Reading files` in the rendered draft; the duplicated `Reading filesRead` no longer appears. The Slack sibling merger applies the identical guard (its dedicated test on this PR head sends the same `Reading files` -> `Read` sequence through the real `dispatchPreparedSlackMessage` and asserts the Slack draft is `Shelling\n• Reading files` with no `Reading filesRead`).
- **What was not tested:** A live Slack desktop rendering of the draft (the `dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts` case drives the real Slack dispatch path with a stubbed Slack client; a maintainer can optionally request a `@openclaw-mantis` Slack desktop smoke using the suggested command if a rendered screenshot is required).

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)

$ pnpm test extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  81 passed (81)

$ pnpm tsgo:core:test
EXIT=0 (type check passed)
```

Added `ignores reasoning deltas that are a substring of the current buffer` to both the shared compositor suite and the Slack `dispatch.preview-fallback` suite (the latter drives the real `dispatchPreparedSlackMessage` and asserts the Slack-visible draft keeps `Reading files` with no `Reading filesRead`).

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended, bounded) - a substring resend no longer duplicates the prefix in the Slack / channel progress draft; extension and snapshot cases unchanged.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config or env surface touched.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No - purely a progress-draft merge predicate.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Yes (bounded) - touches the shared `mergeReasoningProgressText` (affects every channel using the compositor) and the Slack sibling `mergeSlackReasoningProgressText`; both are file-local merge helpers with no public API change.
- Highest-risk area: a channel whose reasoning stream legitimately resends a shorter prefix and expected the old append behavior - but the old behavior was a duplication bug; the new predicate only keeps the longer buffer and waits for the next delta.
- Mitigation: 14 compositor + 81 Slack dispatch tests (incl. the two new substring-resend cases) + node runtime verification on the current head.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)

target.title: fix(config/sessions): narrow reply-session initialization revision to identity fields
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98672. Users observed `reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:main` errors that broke ongoing sessions until the gateway was restarted. The error came from the guarded reply-session initialization path comparing the full persisted session entry between snapshot and commit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initialization guard only needs to detect whether another initializer rotated the session (i.e. changed `sessionId`/`sessionFile`). Comparing the entire entry included volatile fields such as `updatedAt`, `lastHeartbeatSentAt`, `contextBudgetStatus`, pending-delivery metadata, etc. These are legitimately mutated by background heartbeat runners, delivery retries, and other gateway activity, so unrelated metadata changes produced false-positive `stale-snapshot` conflicts.

The change narrows `createReplySessionInitializationRevision` to the identity fields `sessionId` and `sessionFile`, and removes the now-unused `projectSessionEntryForPersistenceRevision` helper. A regression test verifies that non-identity metadata changes no longer conflict.

## User Impact

- Sessions no longer fail with `reply session initialization conflicted` when background activity touches session metadata.
- Real session rotations are still detected and retried as before.

target.title: fix(tools-manager): bound GitHub API release tag JSON response read
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`getLatestVersion` in `src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts` fetches the latest GitHub release tag with an unbounded `await response.json()`. A compromised, misconfigured, or SSRF-redirected GitHub API endpoint could return an arbitrarily large response body, forcing Node.js to buffer the entire payload before parsing and causing OOM on the tools-manager update-check path.

While the GitHub API response for a single release is normally small (<1 KB), the unbounded read is an unnecessary risk in a code path that runs during agent tool setup. The sibling error path already has manual body cancellation, but the success path has no size guard.

## Changes

- `src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts`: replace unbounded `response.json()` with the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper, which enforces the standard 16 MiB provider JSON cap via `readResponseWithLimit`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Unbounded GitHub API JSON response read can cause OOM on oversized response.
- **Real environment tested**: Local `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1`, Node v24.
- **Exact steps**: Start HTTP server serving both normal (~100 B) and oversized (20 MB) JSON payloads. Drive both the old unbounded `response.json()` and the new bounded `readProviderJsonResponse` against the oversized endpoint, then verify the normal endpoint still works.
- **Evidence after fix**:

```
$ node --input-type=module ...

=== tools-manager: bound GitHub API response ===

  Before fix (unbounded response.json()):
    20,971,520 bytes read in 160ms (all 20 MB buffered)

  After fix (readProviderJsonResponse with 16 MiB cap):
    threw: GitHub releases: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes
    (stream cancelled at cap, ~17.5 MB sent vs 20 MB total)

  Normal response (backward compatible):
    v1.2.3 (parsed correctly, unchanged)
```
- **Observed result**: Oversized body is stopped at the 16 MiB cap with a clear error instead of buffering the full 20 MB. Normal responses are unchanged.

## Evidence

```
--- Negative control: oversized GitHub API response (20 MB) ---
  Before: unbounded response.json() → 20,971,520 bytes read (full buffer)
  After:  bounded readProviderJsonResponse → throws at 16,777,216 bytes cap
          → stream cancelled, OOM prevented

--- Verification: normal response (backward compatible) ---
  After:  v1.2.3 (unchanged)
```

**What was not tested**: End-to-end with real GitHub API (requires network). The `node:http` loopback proof covers transport and cancellation behavior.

target.title: fix(minimax): guard music generation SSE JSON.parse against malformed frames
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/minimax/music-generation-provider.ts:266` calls `JSON.parse(json)` on SSE data frames without try/catch. A malformed SSE data frame → unhandled `SyntaxError` → music generation crashes instead of skipping the bad frame.

## Changes

- `extensions/minimax/music-generation-provider.ts`: extract `parseMinimaxMusicStreamFrame()` helper that wraps `JSON.parse` with try/catch → throws descriptive `Error("MiniMax music generation returned malformed SSE JSON frame.")` instead of raw `SyntaxError`. Call site in `readStreamingTrack()` catches and `continue`s (skips bad frame), preserving existing behavior.
- `extensions/minimax/music-generation-provider.test.ts`: two tests verifying the fix (mocked SSE + real HTTP server)
- `test/_proof_minimax_music_json_guard.mts`: standalone proof script that imports and calls the actual `parseMinimaxMusicStreamFrame()` function directly

This follows the same pattern as merged D4 JSON.parse guard PRs: #97889 (discord), #97973 (matrix), #97999 (twilio), #98073 (signal), #98587 (slack).

Label: bugfix | merge-risk: 🟢 minimal | AI-assisted

## Evidence

### Standalone proof script (L2) — calls the ACTUAL exported function

```
$ node --import tsx test/_proof_minimax_music_json_guard.mts

[1] malformed SSE frame JSON → descriptive Error
  PASS  throws Error (not SyntaxError)
  PASS  message includes "malformed SSE JSON frame"

[2] valid MiniMax music frame → returns correctly
  PASS  no error thrown
  PASS  returns object
  PASS  audio hex preserved
  PASS  base_resp.status_code is 0

[3] empty string → throws Error
  PASS  throws Error for empty string

[4] non-object JSON → parses (type check is caller's responsibility)
  PASS  no error thrown for valid JSON string
  PASS  returns the parsed string value

==================================================
  Passed: 9  Failed: 0  Total: 9
==================================================
```

Before (current main): `JSON.parse("NOT JSON {{{")` → raw `SyntaxError` crashes music generation
After (this PR): `parseMinimaxMusicStreamFrame("NOT JSON {{{")` → descriptive `Error: MiniMax music generation returned malformed SSE JSON frame.`

### Real HTTP server test (L2) — vitest + live node:http server

The test starts a real `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1:0`, serves an SSE stream with `data: NOT JSON {{{` followed by a valid MiniMax audio frame, then calls `generateMusic()` via `postJsonRequest` forwarded to the local server through real `fetch()`.
